text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Chromebook Plus Convertible Touch Laptop (XE513C24-K01US) What I love:
1. The screen: clear, large, 3:2 ratio
2. The pen: accurate, responsive, attachable inside the device itself
3. The battery life: 6-7 hours if I'm multitasking--not the worst ever, and at least the battery is consistent
4. Android apps: Kindle, Amazon, Drive, Photos, Snapseed, Gmail, Hangouts, Keep, Google Calendar, OneDrive
5. Security: password locked on boot-up, smart-lock if my cell phone is close by
6. Keyboard: deep travel, large keys

What I hate:
1. No Microsoft Office apps anymore (as of 24 Mar 2017). I had to sideload the apks from my smartphone. They installed and worked great. I think Microsoft is just the punk as usual and revoked their access to Chromebooks.
2. My favorite game on android (Rusted Warfare) will not accept touch input after I join an online game.
3. The battery life is not 10+ hrs
4. Slower charging for a full charge. It takes at least a couple hours for a full charge.
5. No multitasking in tablet mode
6. No desktop icons
7. Swiping gestures in android apps are buggy. Sometimes it recognizes the swipe and sometimes not.
8. KineMaster (the best professional video editing app for Android) force quits every time I try to launch it.
9. Will not read 1080p 60fps video properly from my SD card from my camera. It opens the video and plays a weird rainbow filtered version of my video. It is by no means useful.

Since there are so many negatives... I may be returning this Chromebook.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Chromebook Plus Convertible Touch Laptop (XE513C24-K01US)

Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa OK first off, easy to set up, QR code and automatically updates to latest firmware, conects to wifi (find your wifi network and enter password first time), repeat for as many as needed. Easy to install on outside of house, (nice gutter and other clip attachments are optional, and in some cases worth the cost) but the included bracket is just a few screws and have your phone which you should have already download Blink app to set proper angle and direction of all your cameras.
One option is so far awesome are a set of three solar panels to keep Cameras charged.
I have e two cameras that are high volume notifications and was changing batteries every two to three months. With the solar panels we are past four months. Besides the cost, definitely the cinveniencenif getting ladder, switching batteries, realigning.
Clear pictures, sound is pretty darn good as well. Night shots no complaints. Not great, but clear enough to pick out some details.
A couple cons:
This is for all these types of cameras. To set the motion detection off, need to come from side, a straight on view is hit or miss.
Because of this and other issues, video clips are the end of the interaction. So you see their back.
TURN OFF snapshot option in settings. Otherwise you will get a notification every hour with a composite shot every 24hrs. Have not found a use for that option yet. Maybe for folks watching a boat, pool, or other stationary, but mobile items?
With solar panel 4 stars. Fix straight on issue and five stars.
But for the price I believe one of the best wireless security camera set-ups.
I have used three other's, and if money is an option, thisnis for most people.
Also great for keeping an eye and ear on pets and family members (parents with medical issues). Not as good at being there, but definitely a close second.

text_fidelity_a:
Connectland CL-U2MNHUB-4B 4 Ports USB V2.0 Mini Hub (Black) I bought this hub in tandem with a cooling pad to use my laptop as a desktop replacement; I was running out of USB ports (my laptop only has 3) and this would double that number for less than $10. I wasn't sure if, since this hub isn't powered, I would be able to connect my speakers and cooling pad (both of which are powered over USB) with this hub, but I decided to take a chance and they both work perfectly when connected through the hub. It has exceeded all my expectations. Even better, each port has an on/off switch with LED indicator lights so if you're not using something, you can turn it off without unplugging it from the hub.

Pros
-able to run powered things like a cooling pad (for me, at least; your mileage may vary)
-small so it can be easily tucked out of sight
-on/off switches for each port

Cons
-LED indicator lights (I don't find them distracting because they are so small and don't blink, but some people might)
-removing USB connectors can be a little difficult, but that just means they won't fall out while you're trying to use something
(these are both a little nit-picky, I know, but I really have nothing bad to say about this product)

I've only owned it for a week, so I will update my review if anything changes.
text_fidelity_b: Connectland CL-U2MNHUB-4B 4 Ports USB V2.0 Mini Hub (Black)

Sony RM-EZ4 2-Device Universal Remote with Big Buttons If you have even the most bare-bones entertainment setup, you probable have quite a collection of remotes. They all have their uses but, for the times when you just want to turn on the TV and nothing else, it's nice to have a model like the Sony. Simple, small, easy to use and comfortable even for arthritic hands. Nice big buttons so you can see what to press even in low light.

Setup is a snap - just look up the brand of your TV and/or cable box on the supplied list, type in a four digit code, and you're done.

This is not a learning remote - it can only provide the functions that are pre-programmed into the unit (channel up/down, volume, channel entry via a number, channel recall and mute).

It uses two AA batteries that do not come with the unit. Build quality is very good - better than I expected given the price.

You can also get this in black if you purchase it at the store with the red bulls-eye logo. Amazon has a better price, but only offers it in silver.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I am a big fan of my kindles. I have the kindle keyboard ereaders 1st and 3rd gen , the 2nd gen Fire 8.9" and last year I bought the 6" Fire. I would not have bought this one except that my 6" Fire has gotten glitchy. I have not had problems with any of my kindles before so I chalked it up to just a bad egg.
I was thinking of replacing it when I found this great deal on the lastest 7" Fire. $100 for a tablet is such a deal. $50 is AMAZING!!
There isn't a huge difference other than this one is a little bigger. It was easy to import everything from my old tablet to my new one. My books, photos, songs, even my book marks from Silk. The set up took minutes.
The home page is different, it looks like the ones on iphones with all the apps on the home page. You can group them into smaller collections, you can also upload your own photo to be the wallpaper. I like this better than the carousel. You can also group your books into collections. There is a button so that you can move between applications without them closing out. It will show all the last places you went so you can pick up where you were and just switch screens. This is my favorite new feature, even more than the change with the home screen.
I'm not super fond of Silk but it is less annoying since they did an upgrade.
I have only had one problem: when I was first setting it up, the screen kept freezing. I rebooted it and I haven't had an issue since.
This is just as fast as my 6" tablet. Battery usage seems the same as well. According to the specs this should be a little slower than the 6" with less battery time but I have not noticed a difference. The plastic back feels only a little less durable than my other kindles but I'm not concerned. I feel like I have gotten quite a deal.
The camera isn't really improved since there isn't a flash and the sound quality is the same as well. Movies look great. I'm really happy that I can add a memory card. Movies, music, and audio books use a lot of memory but now I'll have more memory than I need.
You are getting so much for your money. I've never used other brand tablets, I'm not an Apple user. They may or may not be better but are their prices worth it?
I love Prime access for music and videos and that they can be downloaded.
I'm very happy with my new tablet!
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
C2G/Cables to Go Audio Unlimited Premium Indoor/Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, Black (SPK-131U) I was very excited to have a large speaker with bluetooth capability for my Iphone to use outside by the pool. This speaker was a total dissapointment on all levels. Or maybe I just received a lemon.

I thoroughly read the instruction manual - twice - to be certain I was doing everything correctly. When I was finally able to get the bluetooth to work (after having to hold down the button on the speaker until the blue light flashed multiple times, which let me know it was activated), it did work from various locations in my yard without any failures. However, as soon as I would turn off the speaker or my Iphone - I would need to re-initialize the bluetooth as if I were logging in for the very first time. The speaker failed to remember by device and so I'd begin the pressing down of the button, blue lights flashing procedure all over again. Every single time.

So I thought I'd contact the manufacturer/vendor to see if there was anything beyond their "trouble shooting" section of the manual that I might be neglecting. I looked everywhere - the box, the manual, the speaker, everywhere - no contact information whatsoever. Not an email address, phone number, snail mail or Facebook/Twitter address to be found. You buy it - you're stuck with it. The only saving grace is Amazon if you need to return it within the acceptable time frame. But what do you do if you have a problem 6 months down the line?

I installed the batteries, tried out the a/c adapter cord, and even used the 3.5 speaker cable to attach my Iphone and by-pass the bluetooth completely. I just wanted to make sure all of these items would work. But the person who designed this unit must have been having a wonderful time when they decided that in order to plug in anything at all, you need to open the battery compartment door in order to get to the connectors. This is insane and is in no way convenient. To constantly have to remove a door, or have cords hanging needlessly is ridiculous.

The sound quality is acceptable but at the price they're selling it for, you could do far better finding a speaker that has much more to offer. And if you're looking for customer service - keep looking cause it isn't here.
text_fidelity_b: C2G/Cables to Go Audio Unlimited Premium Indoor/Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, Black (SPK-131U)

Case Logic KDH-101 Kontrast DSLR Zoom Holster (Black) Here's the bottom line: I compared this case with the Amazon Basics case, and frankly found the latter to be comparable or even slightly better (at a much lower price).

This is a pretty nice case for a DSLR wearing a zoom lens. I have a Nikon D5300 which I usually pack with a 18-200mm zoom lens on it, and have found the Amazon case to be satisfactory for holding the camera+zoom and the lens hood in the main compartment, and the battery charger and of course a spare chip in the side pckets. There's room in a side pocket to carry a small card reader if I want to bring that as well.

The Case Logic case is very similar, and if I had gotten it first I would probably have been quite satisfied. However, I found that the suspension "hammock" for the camera didn't work quite as well in practice as it does in theory. The camera isn't symmetric of course, and more of it seems to slip through the hole than is intended, and it lies in it at an angle. I also found that I couldn't quite as easily put the lens hood on top as I have gotten used to doing with the Amazon case.

Otherwise, this is well made, with sturdy looking and smoothly functioning zippers, robust strap & handle, and functional side pockets. Certainly a good product, you won't regret buying this case, other than possible regret over the price paid. (Note that I haven't owned the cases long enough to comment on any durability differences.)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System I bought my Bose Solo 15 at another online retailer during a one day sale for a price that made it irresistible and after a month, I am happy that I did it. We have two 55" televisions and the one in our master bedroom has the Denon sound base under it and that unit has simply been outstanding. I was actually looking to just buy a second Denon for the living room tv and chose this Bose unit due to the one time sale and the Bose reputation.

This unit sits directly under our 55" Vizio smart tv and connects with the digital audio optical cable - just like the Denon base. I turned off the tv's physical speakers and let the Bose take over. The sound is full and significantly improved over the thin tv speakers. The unit shines when watching movies that have lots of rich soundtrack music and when you use the Dialogue button to soften background sounds and highlight conversation type dialogue.

The Bluetooth connected with my LG V10 phone and my fourth generation Fiire tablet immediately, allowing me to play music and my audio book through the Bose. Very nice extra functionality - the Denon does this as well. The Bose includes a universal remote control that requires some effort to set up correctly and completely. However! Once the cursing and hair pulling was over, I got it done. The Bose remote now operates our television, the Bose base, and our TiVo/cable box exactly as the cable remote does.

My one star deduction is because the only way to use the Bose Solo is with their included remote control. There are no physical buttons on the machine and that strikes me as a real design flaw. If you break or lose this proprietary remote you cannot even turn the Bose on or off, much less actually use it for sound. At least the Denon sound base can be operated manually or trained to respond to other remote controls with three steps. For me this Bose Solo is worth the price I paid (under three hundred bucks) and it is equal to the Denon in sound quality. But for overall value and ease of use, the Denon is the five star product.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System

Lexar NM600 M.2 2280 NVMe 480GB Solid-State Drive (LNM600-480RBNA) Modern computers are a lot more reliable than computers from 10 or 20 years ago. Computers are not getting a lot faster every year like they used to. I no longer replace my computer every couple of years. If your computer is getting a little sluggish, instead of replacing the whole thing, you can usually give it a huge performance boost by upgrading just key components. In particular, upgrade your memory and upgrade your hard drive. This SSD does not add a lot of capacity, but it gives you a lot of speed so that programs or databases that you use a lot will load much more quickly.

This drive installed and formatted easily on my Windows 10 desktop computer. It's been running flawlessly since then and the performance is great for me. Performance is great for general-purpose home or business use.

There are a lot of different SSDs on the market these days. Check your computer manufacturer's website to see what is compatible with your motherboard. This SSD has an entry-level design and a budget price to match. High-performance SSDs designed for hard-core gaming or video editing can be twice as fast but also cost twice as much or more for the same capacity.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar NM600 M.2 2280 NVMe 480GB Solid-State Drive (LNM600-480RBNA)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I received a Kindle as a gift, and it has taken over my reading life. I'm sad when a book is only available in print and delighted when there is a Kindle version. It's not AS comfortable as a print book, it's MORE comfortable than a print book. The font is amazing. It's easy to use, and for people who knit, it sits nicely in a bookstand on or a reader's pillow to read while knitting.

I have the Sony eReader. I used to own the rocket. I see the Kindle as the real future of ebooks, and I really want ebooks to succeed for a few reasons.

One is storage. If you are a bibliophile, you probably have a book army ready to take over your home. We avid readers are forced to cull our libraries to make room for new books. No more. I would suggest opening a free account with a service like Goodreads to categorize books, since with the Kindle you can't set up a "history" section and a "fantasy" section, but that's so minor. I never could keep those organized in my print library as well, and many books fall into multiple categories anyway. Do I need to mention that ebooks don't yellow and decay over time?

Two is portability. If you are the type to carry many books at once (I am--some for study and some for pleasure reading along with a newspaper) then this is the easiest way to do it.

Three is the glorious possibility that books will never go "out of print" again, because there is no "print" overhead, just a little meg sitting in a several terrabyte raid array somewhere. Books will always be a minute away.

Four is the idea that books will be instantly large print and still small, and easy to tote around. My eyes are still quite good, but I'd love to think, when age degrades them someday, I'll still be able to read the latest releases easily.

Five is the instant availability of hot books. When Brisingr came out, it was sitting on my Kindle that morning. Compare that to the sometimes day-long wait we went through for the Harry Potter books (and books that size are yet another reason ebooks rock). I love having the New York Times delivered, but can't stand it when the delivery boy loses the key and rings my bell at 4 in the morning. This is the best of both worlds.

Six is the ease of reading large online documents, such as those from Gutenberg or a friend's novel (and don't we all have someone who sends us large files to read from time to time?)

Seven is the price of the books. Everything is cheaper on the Kindle and some books are frighteningly inexpensive. I bought the Talmud for 99 cents. A collection of the first five books in the John Carter on Mars series for 99 cents. And the entire collection of the Wizard of Oz books for, you guessed it, 99 cents.

Other e-readers hit close to the mark; the Kindle got it right. I only want two things. I want color and I want Amazon to hit that goal of having every book (including comics and manga please) available for the Kindle. Overall, the day of the ebook truly arrived with the Kindle and I couldn't be happier.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed) I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review.

First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything.
Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die.
I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that.
I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb.

I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs.
This one is different.
First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had.
It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable.

it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit.
It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote.
There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey...

My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB.
That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare.
I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up.
We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had
will fit this one. *bang head on desk*
The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own.
I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move
a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough.

This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could.
But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk.

Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet.
But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts.
Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.
text_fidelity_b: HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed)

text_fidelity_a:
OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black) I bought this cover and the Zing Pro Zoom cover. I like the Op Tech D Pro Zoom better.
Pros:
It was easier to get on and off my camera then the Zing.
It fits my camera and accessories nicely.
Seems well made. I have many other Op Tech products that I purchased and they have all held up nicely.
Cons:
To securely close the cover, there is a flap that has 2 snaps. You wrap the cover around the back of the camera, and snap the flap closed with the 2 snaps. I'm not a fan of snaps. These were easy to snap closed, but Velcro would have been much easier.
There is a strap attached to the inside of the cover. It came with 2 ways of attaching the cover to your camera so you don't lose the cover:
1. a piece of leather that attaches to the camera by screwing it into the tripod mount. This piece attaches to the strap with a snap. I could see either end of the leather coming apart - the side with screw could detach or the snap could release.
2. A ring that can go around the lens. This ring attaches to the strap with a snap. I don't like having things attached to my lens and the snap could release.
I came up with my own method of securing the cover to my camera. The bottom of my battery grip has a connection point for a strap. I had an extra set of Op Tech Uni Loop connectors (https://www.amazon.com/OP-TECH-USA-1301062-Uni-Loop/dp/B0010HA6A6/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1485137755&sr=8-1&keywords=optech+uni+loop).
I attached one end to the bottom of the battery grip. I attached the other connector to the strap by looping the strap thru the connector loop and snapping the two snaps on the strap together. Using the uni loop connectors, I clicked the two pieces together. I think the weakest point is where the snaps are attached. I'm going to sew a few stitches next to the strap as a precaution in case the snaps come undone. You can use any type of strap to secure the cover to the camera. I also attached a photo using an extra camera strap from one of my point and shoot cameras. If I used this method, I would still sew a few stitches next to the snap. I like the uni loop method. If the cover gets in the way, I can just disconnect the uni loop clips.
I'm happy with this cover even though I'm using a different method of attaching the cover to my camera. I dropped the rating to a 4 because of the use of the snaps.
text_fidelity_b: OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue Note: I would love to love this speaker set, but it has inconsistent performance with various devices. I received a review sample and was pleased by the sound when I plugged this into the phone port on my ThinkPad T61. The sound was clear and I could hear every note on the album that I use to test speakers (Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B000002ADT Kind of Blue]]). I use that album because the instruments in the ensemble cover low, mid and high range frequencies. The bass was a little thin, but with the speakers less than two feet away the sound was rich and I was happy.

Where I started to experience problems was when I plugged this into the 3.5mm port on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone. There was static in the mix. The same with my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] - static interfered with the music. My final test was to plug the 3.5mm cable end into an [[ASIN:B00AEJJRBK Avantree Cara Bluetooth 4.0 Handsfree stereo Car Kit with mic]] and connect via bluetooth. The sound was crystal clear.

I am not sure what conclusions to draw. It could be something wrong with the Samsung phone and tablet, although both work perfectly with headphones which I have directly plugged into their 3.5mm ports. It may be that the 3.5mm cable and interface on the input of this speaker is overly sensitive to impedance and the slightest deviation will induce static. I am not sure, but because I was unable to get the same quality consistently across all devices with which I tested these speakers I subtracted two stars.

Construction is exceptional, although I wish the design employed removable USB and 3.5mm cables instead of the fixed ones that provide power and signal inputs, and connect the two units. As it stands if a cable breaks it will take some skill to repair it. With removable, off-the-shelf cables a broken one can be rectified with a trip to an electronics store.

Overall, on the two devices that I tested with which these speakers worked the sound was spectacular. On the other two it was unlistenable. If you are connecting this to a bluetooth receiver it's probably a safe choice, but if you are connecting this to anything else I would proceed with caution.
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD) I had high hopes for this docking station from StarTech but, thus far, I’ve been pretty disappointed.

Like many people I like the portability of working from a laptop but when I am at my workstation I want more screen space to work on - I thought this Docking Station would be a perfect solution. Well, in theory, it would.

Inside the box you’ll find the docking station, a 3.0 USB cable, a power adapter with snap on plugs to fit various world power sources, a DVI to VGA adapter, and a CD-ROM.

Unlike many docking stations or hubs this is not Plug and Play. I’m running the most updated Windows 10 64bit and the CD-ROM is completely useless. After inserting it in my computer I received a message reading that it was not compatible with my machine. No problem, I went to the manufacturer’s website, found the product, clicked on support, downloaded the zip file containing the setup and updated drivers for my OS and continued.

I went through the installation process and it appeared to install fine. After accepting the user agreement it checked my system for compatibility - finding no issues it continued and completed installation. I went to device manager and noticed an error in USB connected devices but figured with a restart it would correct.

I restarted but the error remains. Configuration Descriptor Request Failed - Windows has stopped device. I have uninstalled and reinstalled, searched help, used Windows Update to search for a better driver - so far nothing has worked.

In regards to functionality - the USB ports (two 3.0 and four 2.0) all function without issue and the Ethernet Port works great providing me over 200Mb/s. Due to not having the correct drivers I’ve been unable to test the multiple monitor capabilities.

I have contacted tech support and as of writing I have not heard back. If they are able to help me solve these issues I will update my review to reflect my further findings.

It appears this Docking Station is outdated being developed for older operating systems and while it may work for some users, others will find it needlessly difficult.

I would look at more recently manufactured docking stations that have been developed with the current operating systems - especially if you are using Windows 10.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD)

SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.
text_fidelity_b: SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM

Mom and dad love them too, so we can’t really fault the two pre- teens from using and enjoying their electronics to the fullest. We like it best when they are at least devoting some of their electronic time to doing things more constructive and/or creative, and this is what convinced me to get my hands on this SOSUN Camcorder.

I had not heard of SOSUN until I got this camcorder, but I had read good things about the brand and decided that such a large percentage of customers must be right about something. There are better camcorders out there that create better videos and have more features, but this one is still good for a beginner like my 13 year old.

Camcorders can get expensive , especially if your needs and demands are high. But if you’re looking for a good starter camcorder for a very low price, this SOSUN is going to be difficult to match. text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

GreatShield Ultra Anti-Glare Screen Protector Film for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, Kindle Touch, and Kindle Keyboard I bought this screen protector for my Kindle Touch earlier this year and love it. I just bought a Kindle Paperwhite and I had one left over from the first order. It fit perfectly, except the small gap ended up on the top and I did not realize that the line cut through the top of the menu until I turned it on to read. I'd rather have the gap at the bottom where it's not noticeable so I ordered another pack. I just got my order today and after two screens, I realized that they were too wide for the Paperwhite screen. I had to cut the last screen to get it to fit. I was bummed since it fit great before and I thought I'd get it perfect on the first try. I'm not completely happy with the final result but I don't want to pay for another pack not knowing which size I'm going to get. Also the edges used to be rounded and they aren't anymore so I can't get the edges to stick flat to the screen which makes the screen protector more noticeable, whereas on my Kindle Touch, I actually have to look carefully to see where the edges are. I just don't understand why these things changed. I don't know if I got a bad batch but if this is the size they are selling now, they shouldn't advertise that it fits the Paperwhite.
As far as applying, I give that four stars. I can normally get a bubble-free application. If anything goes wrong it's usually a speck of dust. I use compressed air and a credit card to get the best results. A credit card is more solid than the smoothing card it comes with so it works a lot better.

UPDATE 11/18/2012: The GreatShield company responded to my review and they sent me a replacement order right away. Awesome customer service from those guys. After getting my replacement, I can safely say that the order I had before was defective. The new order fit the screen perfectly and the edges are rounded. It is installed on my Kindle Paperwhite and I'm a happy customer. In light of this, I have changed my rating from 2 stars to 5 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics DSLR Camera Backpack (High Density Water-Resistant 840D Polyester) - Ash Gray There is room for my 13" laptop, my 12.9" ipad pro, all my camera lenses and the body for my sony A7ii, snacks, water bottle, and you can attach a tripod to it.

The failure of this camera backpack (along with all others I've tried is that it looks really bulky on my short petite frame ( 5'4" woman). I think it makes me look fatter because of how wide the bag is, I tried it on my guy friend (also a photographer) who I was hanging out with and it looks much better! He really appreciated the hip and chest straps that go across the front for when he's on his motorcycle.

I would definitely use this for travel. Your expensive camera gear can only be retrieved by taking off the backpack since the zipper is next to your back which makes me feel safer. Would be great for carrying everything through the airport and sending your photography equipment through the security scanners.

The hip and shoulder straps really help to distribute the weight of the bag so it's also great for long hikes to get that perfect landscape shot in the mountains. I'm looking forward to trying it out more this summer in the rockies.

TLDR:
Pros:
- color/texture of the bag is really attractive
- has plenty of room for your favorite lenses and mirrorless camera (I don't have a DSLR so couldn't test that)
- can also fit laptop + tablet, charging cables, snacks
- comfortable shoulder straps
- comes with a waterproof bag that fits around the backpack in case you're stuck in bad weather
- camera section is modular which allows you to fit a variety of lenses, I was also able to fit my flash in here.
- GREAT bag for the price. You can't beat $44 for this.
- there are thoughtful interior flaps by your lenses that prevent water from touching them in case if rain gets in by the zipper.

Cons:
- Bulky looking
- could have more pockets instead of two laptop sections.
- If you open bag when its sitting up instead of laying down your camera will fall out
- the interior finishings arent as nice as the outside fabric
- mine was missing the black strap you see in the product photography that holds the camera in vs. having it just sit at the top of the bag.

Overall it's a great bag if you're starting out in photography for traveling and just to store all your gear in one place safely. I think you can't beat the price for this bag and the fabric on the exterior is very attractive. It does get heavy with all your gear in it so I really appreciate the hip straps to distribute the weight.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics DSLR Camera Backpack (High Density Water-Resistant 840D Polyester) - Ash Gray

text_fidelity_a:
USB C Docking Station, UtechSmart 18in1 Quadruple Display Laptop Docking Station for MacBook Pro & Windows,Thunderbolt 3 Dock with SSD Enclosure 3HDMI VGA 100WPD 5USB-A SD/TF Slot 3.5mm RJ45 Everything about this dock is either confusing, misleading, or falsely. First of all, I’m not quite sure I see the point of having two hosts connect to it as I it does not seem to be a like a KVM switch in any way. For one, video output is dedicated to one or the other host depending on the port. There is no switch to toggle between hosts so USB devices seem to be shared? Honestly it’s not at all clear. The power supply also can only charge one host, I believe whichever is plugged in first. Since there is a single ethernet jack that both hosts share it also shares a single MAC ID. The only explanation for any of this seems to be to give a buyer some impression that it behaves like a KVM switch that allows you to share peripherals. In fact it’s not even clear what it does as the instructions are incomplete. Since I was unable to get a keyboard to work connected to it I presume can you either use the built-in keyboard or plug it directly into the laptop.

I honestly didn’t even fully unboxed this thing after reading the instructions and trying to make sense of them. Once I saw that video was not shared and that the resolution was appallingly low, all of the other issues were already moot. It is advertised as a thunderbolt 3 dock but it’s apparent that thunderbolt 3 support is quite limited and it’s really a USB-C dock. Seeing how the function of this device is very unclear a pure its existence only serves to fool customers like me into not having to use a KVM. Since the description and the instructions appear to be deliberately vague, it would seem this is the point. This also explains why it’s so much less expensive than a single host dock or a dual host KVM.

Back to Amazon with you!
text_fidelity_b: USB C Docking Station, UtechSmart 18in1 Quadruple Display Laptop Docking Station for MacBook Pro & Windows,Thunderbolt 3 Dock with SSD Enclosure 3HDMI VGA 100WPD 5USB-A SD/TF Slot 3.5mm RJ45

The not so good: lens is cheaply made, plastic abounds and is fragile. Lens creep is insane and the little switch that locks it back doesn't work half the time, the other half you're quickly struggling to find the tiny switch it to unlock your lens to shoot a fleeting shot of a genuine alien spacecraft flipping off tourists in Tahiti.

Broke the zoom (internally) two-days after landing in Phuket, Thailand (luckily it was for an underwater shoot with GoPros). Took eight-weeks for Thailand to get the parts and fix it at the genuine Canon service center. The knackered cheap plastic internal parts they replaced and were so gracious to give me the originals back, do NOT inspire confidence in reliability. If you don't use the lens and keep it stored in a box, it should last a long time for you. If you actually use it..., beware!
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 18-200mm f/3.5-5.6 IS Standard Zoom Lens for Canon DSLR Cameras

Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27 We can not find the remote for our Roku or downstairs TV which is a Samsung since we had to remodel over a long period of time due to a flood which started it all. I thought this would be perfect.

BUTTONS
The layout and buttons of this remote are pretty small. They are not difficult to use, however. The explanation in the instructions is pretty good.

USING WITH SAMSUNG AND ROKU
I have an older Samsung TV and a Roku Premiere hooked up to it. At first this worked fine with the TV, but the Roku it just would not work. Finally, I hit the SET UP button and held it until it blinked. I used the S button (next to the TV button) and suddenly instead of having to program the Roku, it just started to work. I did not have to enter roku codes at all.

DOES IT WORK WITH BOTH WELL?
Both of those things work well. I might try to set up DVD later, but for now, all I really wanted was to have the Roku and TV to work. I have a separate satellite remote that I use for DISH so I am not that interested in using this for that as it is upstairs. I would love a Sleep button like my other Samsung remote has, but really that is not a big deal for this particular TV.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For me, once I put in the two AAA batteries, this remote took almost no time to set up for my older Samsung TV and Roku Premiere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish this had a sleep setting to it, but that is minor. It does what I want it to and runs both Roku and Samsung TV nicely.
text_fidelity_b: Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27

EPN Laptop Stand, Adjustable Laptop Riser with USB Cooling Fan, Ergonomic Computer Stand for Desk, Compatible with MacBook Pro Air, Dell, HP, Lenovo, More 9-16" Laptops, Aluminium Silver The EPN adjustable laptop stand is constructed of heavy-duty aluminum and feels sturdy. I tried it with both my 2017 15" Intel MB Pro and the redesigned 2020 16" MB Pro with a thicker bottom case.

I tend to lean my hands on the edge of my laptop, so I found the rise on the edge to be somewhat high when using it with my older computer, although I do appreciate having the extra fans for cooling on that model because Intel Mac Books Pro models tend to overheat.

This stand can handle the weight of both machines, with the latter coming in at over 4lbs, along with the weight of my hands leaning on it, and there was no indication of it wanting to sag or sink in any way. It will stay put at whatever angle or height you choose. At least it did for me.

I like having a slight angle when I type, and being able to raise my screen's camera to eye level so I am not looking down at it during Zoom meetings for that double chin effect. It's also convenient to have that little nook of space to tuck any cables and SSDs underneath, and out of the way.

There is about an inch to two inches of overhang on either side with larger computers, but it's not much, and both computers felt stable.

Overall, I would say it's a very good, and high-quality laptop stand. However, it is a bit smaller than I expected.
text_fidelity_b: EPN Laptop Stand, Adjustable Laptop Riser with USB Cooling Fan, Ergonomic Computer Stand for Desk, Compatible with MacBook Pro Air, Dell, HP, Lenovo, More 9-16" Laptops, Aluminium Silver

Then you can connect an ethernet cable from any one of the lan port of your primary router into anyone of the lan port of this Netgear. One thing I'm not clear on, and I'll have to contact Netgear and ask them... is whether or not, I can still use the SIM LTE back-up if the Netgear is set as an extension. text_fidelity_a:
C. Crane CCRadio-2E Enhanced Portable AM FM Weather and 2-Meter Ham Band (Black) CC2BE To mention right off the bat, I am not even an amateur radio operator, just someone who enjoys radio. I find radio to be far more romantic and compelling than modern methods of broadcasting. Staying up late in the night and turning the dial with the soft glow of the tuner, the sound of static and mystery that can sometimes accompany radio broadcasts offers something truly genuine that you can't get anywhere else today. That feeling is priceless and not duplicable (If that was even a word).

Anyway, this radio is good quality and contains the capability needed to reach further than most others. If you enjoy radio as I do, a clock radio, ghetto blaster or home stereo won't cut it. If you know what I am talking about, then this radio is for you. I've stayed up many nights listening to Coast to Coast AM on the internet, but it lacked the feeling something like this radio will bring you. I was unable to pick up a station on my home stereo to listen to CTC and was forced to use the internet. The internet provided a clear, stereo sounding broadcast and was very clear.

The CC Radio has been spoken about on the program for many years. I finally picked one up and am very pleased with it's performance. I can now pick up the radio broadcast of Coast to Coast AM and with all the nuances I expect of a a late night radio broadcast. When interesting speakers talk about compelling topics, a crystal clear internet broadcast does not move you inside. However, using the CC Radio, the slight static, the slight fading in and out and all other fantastic experiences you can only receive using a real radio, it has the ability to make you feel and even send chills up your spine. There is just something a good solid radio can do for you that nothing else can and the CC Radio delivers on that 100%.

You will not be disappointed and I really need to get my license.
text_fidelity_b: C. Crane CCRadio-2E Enhanced Portable AM FM Weather and 2-Meter Ham Band (Black) CC2BE

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic True Wireless Earbuds | Bluetooth Earbuds|IPX4 Water Resistant | Small, Lightweight | Long Battery Life, Alexa Compatible | RZ-S300W (White) I've been a fan of Panasonic's consumer electronics since their camcorder days, so I was excited to try these! I've owned many of the cheap Chinese wireless earbuds, and generally sound is good enough for music or listening to videos but I've never found one with a microphone decent enough for sound quality outside of the major brands (Apple, Samsung, etc).
Well, I'm happy to say these Panasonic 'buds don't skimp! They don't cost as much as the big players but the sound quality both for listening and microphone use is head and shoulders over the cheap knock offs. The noice cancelling feature is pretty amazing as well, and overall I'm very pleased with the feature set and quality of those features. But here's the caveat:
The ergonomics aren't great. Touch sensitive buds are difficult for me because I'm the kind of person who moves around a lot and needs to adjust my earbuds to keep them from falling out. But touch sensitivity means sometimes I'm accidentally activating things when I don't want to. I also didn't find some of the features intuitive and had to learn how to use them properly (changing noise cancelling modes for example). They also have rather bright blinking LEDs but you'll only notice that in a dark room. All in all, this is a good product that could be made better in a second edition. For the price, I think it fits squarely between the polished big name brands and the cheap knock offs. This is a good product, it works and doesn't exactly what it says. But it isn't perfect.

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic MSEC-2 EVA Molded Compact Camera Case (Blue) Don't expect this case to be a hard shell case. It's certainly harder than the soft, padded cases but it can be easily bent back and forth with little pressure. There is no padding on the inside so therefore nothing but the case shell and your camera to absorb shock if it's dropped. I wouldn't feel particularly good about dropping my camera while inside this case, but it would be better than no case at all.

Despite the shell of the case being made of plastic, it is not waterproof since water can seep in around and through the zipper which begins at the bottom of the case and goes all the way around back to the bottom again. There is a mesh pouch on the inside of the case but I find little room is left after my regular sized digital camera is placed inside the case to have much space left for something to be placed in the mesh pouch. I don't think the pouch will hold much except for maybe very flat items such as an extra card or flat battery. I can't close the case with my camera (Fuji EXR) and 2 AA batteries inside. I have to take the batteries out. It won't hold a Flip recorder or any camera bigger than a flat digital.

I don't understand the nonadjustable lanyard either. I don't want to wear this case around my neck and there is no way to secure it onto a belt or belt loops. And it's not all that easy to quickly get your camera out when you need to take a fast picture and even more difficult to put it back into it's case. It always takes two hands. At least it won't fall all the way open because it has a an elastic strap on both sides (secured from the inside) to prevent it from opening up completely. Your camera isn't likely to fall out immediately but will eventually if you don't close it back up.

Nice color though....I really like the deep ocean blue color.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic MSEC-2 EVA Molded Compact Camera Case (Blue)

AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+ FD4100WMGUSBX My old computer was exactly that: Old! It needed some serious work. I was running an Athlon X2 6000+ and an EVGA 9800GT. It was a great system back in the day! But, time took its toll. I was kicking around the idea of getting an Intel i3, since they seem to edge out this chip, and are competitively priced (I never overclock my equipment, so it's at stock settings.) But the future upgradability seemed like it'd be very costly. Over all, this chip performs just fine. I mainly upgraded so I could play Diablo 3, and with an EVGA 550 Ti, I play it on high settings, and it looks as good as I could want it to look. My old machine did just fine with standard productivity stuff, but I wanted to play games that were more recent than WoW. I'm able to do everything I want, with no signs of a lag. If I need to upgrade, I'm banking that the next generation of this chip will see some improvements (though the improvement I'm seeing from my last CPU is leaps-and bounds!) The AM3+ socket will be around for a while. Over all, this is a great chip, and easy on the wallet.

**Update 9/6/12**
I recently purchased Guild Wars 2. The game is fairly CPU-intensive, but the FX-4100 keeps up just fine! I think I'm sitting at around 50% plus load at any given time during actual game play on all four cores. I haven't had a single hiccup or spot of lag yet!

Starcraft 2 is another CPU-heavy application, and coupled with the 550 Ti card, I'm running it on Extreme at 1400x900 resolution, and it's flawless. Again, all four cores are loaded, and quite frequently, they're over 60%. Things get a little warm (35C or so) when compared to when I run other applications. Nothing to worry about!

I have also paid quite a bit of attention to how it runs with Diablo 3. It only uses 2 cores at about 50% load at any given time. That game is more GPU-intensive. I am still very happy with my purchase!

ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem | Approved for Comcast Xfinity, Cox, Charter Spectrum, & more | Two 1 Gbps Ports | 1 Gbps Max Internet Speeds | 4 OFDM Channels | 2 Year Warranty,White I replaced a large bulky router/modem combo from my ISP with this modem, as I already had a good router and didn't need two routers. My ISP was charging roughly $10 a month for their equipment, which I will save now. Of course the SB8200 is a little bit pricey, so it will take me about one and half years to recover my cost. I was surprised how small this modem is; very compact and easy to find space for. It generates a little heat, but has vent holes all over the outside and top for good ventilation. Most of heat come out the top, but obviously you don't want to block any of the openings and make sure there is plenty of space above it. I am getting great speed from the modem and had no issues with it at all. My ISP was able to set it up remotely in about 30 minutes. All the "experts" say it is best to have your own equipment, rather than rent from an ISP. I like that idea, but the only problem is that if equipment fails, you are responsible for it, whereas if you rent from the ISP, they replace any defective equipment at no cost. Also if you need an equipment upgrade, the ISP covers that too. I don't expect to need an upgrade as this will handle the fastest speeds being offered now by my ISP (1 Gbps), although not yet in my area. Right now I have 300 Mbps and the modem handles it nicely without any problem. This modem does NOT use the Puma chipset, which was causing some issues. This is a great
piece of equipment and suitable for home or business. Just has 4 lights (power on, upload, download and connected to internet). I thought I had seen comments about the lights being dim, but they are nice and bright; maybe bright enough to almost be distracting at times. Am very happy so far with the modem and would buy one again if it lasts well over time. There are a couple other modems by other quality manufacturers that are somewhat comparable to this one, but in side by side comparisons this seems to rate a little better. The Arris brand was recommended to me and it is the brand used by my ISP.
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem | Approved for Comcast Xfinity, Cox, Charter Spectrum, & more | Two 1 Gbps Ports | 1 Gbps Max Internet Speeds | 4 OFDM Channels | 2 Year Warranty,White

Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R) At the price (about $40 on Amazon), I expected more from these PIONEER ACTIVE IN-EAR WIRELESS HEADPHONES WITH INTEGRATED CLIP (Red SE-CL5BT(R)). The sound is very clear, which is obviously the most important thing. However, I find the controls (3 tiny, flat buttons) to be fumbly and difficult to use. The fact that the buttons have dual functions (e.g., one button increases the volume when pressed once, and advances music to the next track when pressed and held) is partly to blame. However, the buttons seem slow to respond, so I am constantly pressing and holding when all I want is the press once function.

The headphones paired with both my iPad Pro and my Galaxy S7 smartphone, but NOT particularly easily. To place the headphones in pairing mode, so that your Bluetooth device can see the Pioneer broadcast in the device Settings, you must press and hold the headphones’ center button until a miniscule LED light on the side of the clip blinks alternately red and blue. (Normally, the light is red when the headphones are charging, and slowly-blinking blue when the headphones are turned on and connected.)

What’s hard about that pairing, you may ask? It’s in the instructions, except that the instructions are printed in type so tiny that even the best eyes will need a magnifying glass to read them. Worse yet, the key instructions are printed in pale gray (like grayed-out PC menu selections) on soft, recycled paper that is also gray. Purchasers deserve instructions that are printed in black ink, at the very least.

The clip is nice to have. The battery life isn’t great (about 8 hours), and the battery takes about 2 hours to charge via the included USB cable. The “carrying case” for the extra ear tips (you get size S, M, and L sets) is a small resealable plastic bag. The headphones don’t have “over ear” fit (as stated at least once on the product page), but are strictly “in ear” fit (i.e., battery-powered earbuds).

I didn't try using these earphones to answer telephone calls. However, considering how many mistakes I make with the tiny buttons when playing music, I suspect that I'd be hanging up a lot when I was trying to take calls.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R)

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth This is the second "Creative" brand wireless bluetooth speaker with microphone, and so far, the sound quality has not been very good. The first, "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone" was $127.04 (list price $149.99), and this one currently has a list price of $199.99. I cannot hear any discernable difference in sound quality, though this speaker is larger than the other. They are both OK for being usb powered, but there are better-sounding products out there for the same price if you are willing to sacrifice the speaker option.

I ran the same tests on this speaker as the other and got identical results:

This one gets a mixed review for the overall sound quality, but it does have some features that make it very useful. I will be reviewing its various features individually so you can better assess if this meets your needs or not. I used a decibel measuring app on my phone to determine when the speakers began to distort some of what I played.

Playing audio with Bluetooth or via USB with a computer:
-There is no noticeable difference with playback using Bluetooth versus USB connection to a computer, and it has a Very long range (I walked about 25ft away and it was still doing fine)

AUDIO

75 DECIBELS AND UNDER:
Almost all audio was fine: clear, undistorted, and with pretty good clarity (don't expect GREAT quality or clarity. Just Good.) Some types of music fared poorly even at this relatively soft volume. I used "Fortuna from Carmina Burana" to test the system's limits. (YouTube the piece if you want to know which song I refer to--you'll recognize it immediately) The chorus of singers sounded distorted. At higher volumes, even as lot as 85db, it was awful. Other types of music were fine (orchestra music, pop, hip hop, electronica), but sometimes the treble was a bit fuzzy.

75-85 DECIBELS:
This is the maximum volume the speakers can reach with the USB connection, so it can get loud enough for a small-medium party, but not Very loud.
It's hit and miss here. The treble and bass have some problems, especially treble. The clarity diminishes and any nuances in your music will generally get a bit lost or muffled. Choral music, music with higher pitched percussive elements, and some types of rock and orchestra music don't sound very good.

PHONE CALLS:
The voice of the person you are calling sounds a bit muffled--definitely not as good as headphones or the phone, but about on par with other Bluetooth systems I've tried.

The voice of the speaker (i.e. You) is actually clear! This part gets a solid review. With my built-in car Bluetooth system, as well as detachable ones I've reviewed, usually the person you are calling has trouble hearing you and can experience interference. Maybe that is because it is in the car and there's road noise, but in any case, the fact this one does, actually, sound clear to the recipient of your phone call is a BIG plus.

Overall, this is a good product when you compare it to other desktop laptop speakers. If you are comparing it to products specifically meant for enjoying audio, however, I would recommend the Pioneer Electronics Audition Series for a relatively inexpensive but high quality experience, or Bose if you are looking for something higher-end. The price of the Pioneer product is almost the same, and while it doesn't have Bluetooth unless you buy the attachment separately (about $70) and it only docks with the older iPhone and iPods, the sound quality of that one is stunning. If you want extra features like FREE Bluetooth and speakerphone capability, this one is ok for the price. Not great. Just ok.

Because this is basically the same as the "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone", and the other is about $70 cheaper, I would recommend getting the SBX10 and saving your money. They are basically the same thing, so either pay more and get better sound quality with another product entirely, or pay less for the same thing.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - Wireless - Bluetooth - USB, Bluetooth

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC P402BT Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Integrated Mic, A2DP/AVRCP, 30-Hour Playback for Tablet/Smartphone/MP3 - Black These are pretty good bluetooth headphones. They excel with regard to comfort - the ear padding is plush and they have a nice balance between grip (e.g., staying put when you move) and comfort. The headband consists of 2 plastic rods without any padding, but doesn't cause a significant comfort issue.

I had zero problems pairing these with a couple of different tablets (Android operating system and the Fire version of Android). Simple, quick and painless. The operating range is also excellent, with zero dropouts at about 20 feet and only minor dropouts at 25+ feet.

The sound quality is quite good. While these open-ear designs don't have the booming bass quality of closed designs, I found the sound quality to be very good, especially in the midrange. They are an excellent choice for movie watching since the dialogue comes through so clearly.

I like the operating controls, especially the volume switch. It's a rocker-type design, so it's very easy to use without having to look at the button - just find it by feel, and press up to increase volume and down to decrease. The multifunction button is in the middle of the rocker switch and is very easy to find by touch as well.

The overall look is very snazzy, and the build quality appears solid.

There is only a modest amount of sound isolation, but that again is an issue inherent with open-ear headphones. It does cut ambient sound reasonably well - I had no problems listening to music while on a noisy treadmill without the ambient sound interfering to any significant degree.

Misses are the volume level. These have a rather limited upper volume range. Normally I set my tablet to about the 75% level and the headphone level to close to the upper point to get a good volume that blocks out ambient noise. With these, however, I had to set the tablet sound level to 100% and the earphone level also at 100%, and I still found them a bit lacking in volume. Given the price point, the range should be better.

But other than the volume issue, no complaints. Good sound, good comfort, great range and easy-to-use controls. Well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC P402BT Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Integrated Mic, A2DP/AVRCP, 30-Hour Playback for Tablet/Smartphone/MP3 - Black

We're using this in our kitchen to turn on sofit and undercounter lighting when anyone walks in (very cool, btw). We used X10 for years without a problem but really wanted to integrate this into our new SmartHub/Things setup.

Installing any Ecolink product is a little frustrating since the instructions are merely: plug it in and follow your controller manufacturer's instructions for adding a device. text_fidelity_a:
eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee I contacted Eufy after the battery died after 4 weeks. Took them 2 days to send me an autobot emailed response to which I responded that I wanted a live person to email me. Another 2 days, and a person asked me to send a screen shot of the battery settings. REALLY??? So I did that which my battery settings were for optimized battery life. Another 2 days and still no answer. There was an option on the bottom of their email to escalate the case to management if I was not happy with the response, and that they would get back to me within 24 hours. So I clicked it, and explained how I was not getting a response. But guess what? I never got a response. So five days later, I decided to return this because I'm still in the return window. Maybe I had a defective unit. We have had a very mild winter, so I cannot imagine that the weather would make a supposed four-month battery charge only last for four weeks. Plus, there isn't much motion going on to drain the battery either. Sometimes, 3 or 4 days go by with no motion. The most number of times it has detected motion in one day is four times. So it's not like the battery is getting drained from the camera being triggered 10 times a day. I'm going to try one more time, and watch the battery life to see how quickly it drains before the return window closes.

**** Update **** The replacement camera will have a battery life of approximately 6 or 7 weeks, judging by the amount of battery used thus far. Since the return window is just 4 weeks, I have returned this camera again and will not try another one. 6-7 weeks battery life is better than 4 weeks, for sure. But still disappointing because Eufy advertises a 4 month battery life. I would have been willing to try to Eufy 2 Pro that has a 365-day battery life (figuring it probably really only has a 6 month battery life). But this would mean purchasing a home base. Also, the location of the camera does not get any direct sunlight, so even a solar panel would not have helped. If you are looking for just one camera that is wireless, and you aren't interested in having to take it down every month or two for recharging, this is not the camera for you. Their customer support contacted me the day after I wrote my first review. (I couldn't get any support previously through their normal channels.)
text_fidelity_b: eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

One reviewer mentioned software loading problems. I had absolutely no problems on a Windows 7, 64bit OS.

You can't go wrong with this device. It's an excellent camera for you or the kids or the g-kids for Xmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card)

Anyway, it's super easy to use the app and was super easy to set up these 4 little items. I used the card for my purse, the tile with the key chain hole for my car key fob and the 2 little button tiles for 2 of my TV remotes.

The point of this review is: you should know that you can buy just 1 of these things and finding your phone is an added free feature! Score! I thought I'd have to attach one of those buttons to the back of my phone, but nope! So all you do is double tap the Tile logo on any tile and it will locate my phone anywhere within bluetooth range. This is so totally awesome. I don't have to log into a computer to find my phone and I don't have to stress out looking for it when my partner's not home to ring my phone from her phone. All you have to do is double tap ANY Tile you own in bluetooth range and it'll ring your phone. How great is that???!! Can't find my phone? Grab any remote and double tap the logo - BAM! Can't find my phone? Grab my purse and double tap the logo on the card Tile - BAM! Really an A+ feature that Tile should really be clearer about when advertising their products..... like first thing.

My review doesn't include how you find things when you're out of bluetooth range..... but I think there's an alert for your phone when you're about to leave your wallet somewhere, etc., or about to exit bluetooth range.... pretty sure that's how it works. Anyway, just finding my phone and things around the house will save me how many search minutes (hours) a year??? And garners a 5 star rating on that alone.

It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US

The inside diameter of the cable lug hole is 0.331in. or 8.4mm and I noticed it does have a significant burr on the inside of the hole, thus reducing the inside diameter somewhat.  This burr when crimping will keep wire from being placed in the hole and bite the copper some during the crimp, abrading the wire. The slip-on insulation is easy to slide on and off the terminal so the cable should be easy to install. There is a large letter "L" and "R" on the inside of the headphones. They adjust about an inch on each side. The top and the ear piece are padded and very comfortable. The ear pieces rotate about 90 degrees, and they can be folded in. There is an audio jack, a mini usb port, a volume increase and decrease button, pause button, noise cancelling activation button, and power button. The volume button controls the volume on the device you have it connected to. When you press the volume button, for some reason the media stops for a second then adjusts. The true test was turning on my tv with my sound bar on (and it's a really good one) and I kept turning it up and didn't hear a thing. I took these headphones off and my tv was blaring, so much so that my sub woofer was vibrating the bed, but I didn't hear a thing. So, these are DEFINITELY noice cancelling.

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple) There's a lot to like about the Playsport. For one, it's very easy to use as a point and shoot should be. The picture quality is certainly fine for just about anybody's use, save for those who really like blowing their pictures up large. It's very fast to move between photos and movie--a few thumb moves is all it takes. The same for toggling between the movie quality. Which means if you suddenly want to grab a still photo while videoing or are worried about recording room and want to drop down a notch or two in quality, you can do so without missing a lot of action. The zoom is a 3X, which is serviceable. I'd prefer longer and I'm sure the next version will offer a longer zoom, but as I use this for quick shots of the family and not for event shooting, the 3X is rarely an issue in terms of not being adequate.

Transfer of files is easy and fast (I use a Mac) and all the cables come bundled with it. Yes, you read that right--it ships with all the needed cables.

Because it is so small and slim, and held in that vertical position, it can get a bit shaky and you'll need to pay attention to keeping it steady, more so than larger cameras or ones you hold with two hands horizontally. The sound pickup is fine save that wind noise can be a problem on windy days--it'll wash out a good deal of the speaking sound.

It feels rugged out of the box and the number of times I've dropped it, including just recently while chasing my boy and his friend around the corner of the house and getting my foot caught in the extension cord of the Halloween decorations. I watched the camera skid across several feet of concrete sidewalk but it was none the worse for wear.

It's slimness makes it a great pocket camera--one of those where it's defined as such not because you can cram it into your pocket and walk around like you have a grapefruit in there but where it slips right in and you barely notice it. That's one of the reasons it's become the camera I take most often when I know I won't need a larger zoom or a flash.

I haven't tried the underwater aspect in actual underwater conditions (snorkeling, say), but a few practice photos in the pool shows it takes pretty sharp photos in that environment. But I'll leave the gauging of that aspect to those more well-versed in such a need.

In the end, it's a great little camera and as mentioned, it's quickly become the one I carry along most often when we're just heading out for some family fun. For post-dusk indoor, I take a Canon elph and for events or hiking a Canon IS with a 12x zoom and a tele-converter. But for playing games in the yard, birthday parties, classroom events, etc.--the Kodak has become the go-to camera.

highly recommended
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White This is an extremely comfortable to wear set of lightweight over-ear headphones.

There's often a lot of noise in my house. A television on somewhere, dishes being done, and a nine year old that never stops talking. I like to use headphones as an escape. When headphones claim they are noise isolating I hold them to it. These headphones did not disappoint me. The nicely cushioned soft pleather covered ear cups adjust for angle to offer a secure fit that provides excellent insulation against ambient noise and are very comfortable to wear, even for extended periods of time.

I found that they could deliver the snap of live instruments, or the impression that I was at a club with the singer on the stage in front of me. When the music had stopped, there was still silence. I noticed that I enjoyed wearing them because of the peace and quiet, I didn't want to take them off actually. These headphones isolate out noise so well they made me consider wearing them when the kid's home just to be able to hear myself think.

The sound quality is crisp, great clarity not overpowering and provide a personal ambience. They offer a great balance and at no point was I confused when watching movies. They were even picking up the weighty and seismic bass from Jurassic Park that would imply a dinosaur was right behind me. The adjustable aluminum headphone band has a slight amount of padding beneath the pleather covered top part, but I wish it had just a little bit more to provide a bit more cushioning. Finally, the headphones are able to smoothly swivel flat for storage or packing although the cable is too long for me to want to use these for trips.

Overall I am incredibly happy with their quality, especially for the price. They're very comfortable, provide excellent noise isolation, and deliver very clean response with deep bass. I plan to enjoy using them and am pleased to recommend them on Amazon.

Retail sample provided at no cost by Edifier for my testing, evaluation, and review.
text_fidelity_b: Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White
