BRAINWAVZ S0 in-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset for iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices (Black) Since there are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews already I will focus on where these phones are best suited. I received mine as a review sample and have been using them for nearly a week to make sure I thoroughly test them.

For me these are best for critical listening, and especially raw mixes if you do recording. Of course they are not limited to that. The fact that these phones are fairly neutral across the entire frequency spectrum makes them ideal for listening to unmixed recordings, as well as music that you are studying or transcribing. The reproduction is so balanced that listening to albums with these compared to other phones - including some other Brainwavz models - is like night and day.

If you are listening to music that is heavily biased towards bass and drums these may not be the best phones for you. If you listen to acoustic music these are near perfect because you can easily hear every note. I tested it on a few jazz albums that I own as well as a broadcast of two friends from a local station that had been recorded directly from the sound board and it was wonderful to hear what was actually recorded versus what a biased pair of phones normally reproduce.

A few notes about comfort: these are light, do a great job of isolating ambient noise without totally eliminating it, and are easy to wear. I am not an IEM (in ear monitor) type of person, but these presented no problems even when I wore them for three to four hours straight. A big plus is this set comes with different sized foam ear pieces and a nice case (the [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]).

While these phones may not be for everybody, they are perfect for those of us who spend a lot of time critically listening to music and/or transcribing it. If you fall into that category you will probably love them.
text_fidelity_b: BRAINWAVZ S0 in-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset for iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I've been using this keyboard and mouse since it arrived on 12/27/16 and it fits my use perfectly. I work from a home office and got a treadmill desk for Christmas and needed a wireless keyboard so I can move it back and forth between the treadmill side and the keyboard tray on the other half of the desk for when I'm seated. I got so used to a split ergonomic keyboard and had difficulty finding this style in a wireless keyboard.

This is low profile enough to fit under the desk when I slide the keyboard tray out of the way. You can use it with or without the very easily magnetic attachable riser to raise the wrist rest; I use it without the riser when on the treadmill and with it when I'm seated so this is a great feature for me. I suppose it is somewhat equivalent to using the legs on traditional keyboards.

A large part of my day is spent on the phone with executives and I often type while talking with people (conducting telephone interviews). This keyboard is so much quieter than my old one! Now people don't even know that I'm typing while speaking with them. It did take me a day or two to get used to the keyboard layout since it is a bit different from my old wired ergonomic keyboard.

The mouse seemed too big initially but now I really like it.

I use the number keypad a lot and having it separate from the keyboard is sometimes not the most convenient. However, if it was attached to the keyboard, the set up would be too big for my keyboard tray and mouse so it is more of a positive than a negative with the new treadmill desk set up.

Overall, I am very happy with it and recommend it wholeheartedly. You will especially like it if you are used to using an ergonomic keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 900VA UPS Desktop Battery Back Up, 12 Outlet, 480W 120V Standby, Ultra-Compact, USB (INTERNET900U) First off, this was purchased for a 27" iMac for home usage.

I changed my previous configuration where my modem, router, NAS and iMac were all located in or on my office desk. These were all connected to a CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD that's been working perfectly for almost 5 years. After moving the location of the modem, router and NAS to a more central location; I moved the CyberPower UPS along with them. This left me for a need for a small UPS for the iMac only.

I originally looked at the smaller Cyberpower UPSs but then looked at the competition. The two I had narrowed it down to were similar in price, but the Tripp Lite offered a larger battery capacity. I then looked at their listings and found the Origin listed under the Product Information. The Tripp LIte stated that it was Made in USA or Imported while the Cyberpower was listed with a China origin. A little more searching and Tripp Lite is based out of Chicago. This essentially sealed the deal and the INTERNET 550U was ordered from Amazon.

Much to my disappointment, there was a large label on the side of the box clearly stating MADE IN CHINA. -1 Star

From the Manufacturer section of the listing would have you believe that the PowerAlert Software will work on the Mac OSX. After trying to find the PowerAlert Software from the Trip Lite web site would state the following...

"If you are a home or small office user, PowerAlert Local is for you. It allows you to monitor and control a UPS system connected to your computer through a USB or serial cable. It also supports automatic file saves and unattended computer shutdown during power outages."

Looking below this statement and there is no download availability for Mac OSX. The only Mac OSX software availability is called PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent and it states the following...

"If you need to automate computer shutdown during an outage without a USB or serial connection to a UPS system, or if you can’t use Java, PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent is for you. When it detects a user-selected event (such as low battery) broadcast by a network-connected UPS system, it initiates shutdown or hibernation after a user-defined delay."

Not quite what I was looking for but I did find that the native software within Mac OSX seems to do what I need it to do without the need of installing additional software. -0 Stars

This UPS is considerably light compared to the larger CyberPower. For whatever reason, I was expecting something heavier. It gives the impression that it's cheap in feel. Not necessarily of any fault of the device but some perceived notion that I had. But when coupled with the horrible, plastic smell; it comes off as another characteristic of a cheap, Chinese product. -1 Star

In summary, we had a long power outage last weekend while I was at the computer. The UPS worked as it should, allowing me to shut down the computer.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 900VA UPS Desktop Battery Back Up, 12 Outlet, 480W 120V Standby, Ultra-Compact, USB (INTERNET900U)

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a:
CoolBELL 17.3 Inches Convertible Laptop Messenger Bag Shoulder Bag Backpack Oxford Cloth Multi-Functional Briefcase for Men Women Laptop/MacBook (Blue) First and foremost, I need a convertible backpack which allows for transport - all materials needed for the long days on campus (grad student). In addition, I need the professional aspect to function as a briefcase. Solely on those points, this bag fits the bill. (BTW - no discount or freebie here for this review - I paid for this!)
PROS:
1. Material: feels and looks professional, good color, seems at the very least to be water repellent
2. Zippers: seem strong enough, especially when loaded - two of them house the briefcase handles
3. Padding: quality - on the backpack straps and particularly the section directly meant for the computer
4. Compartments: although the pictures do not necessarily show this, there are zippers on the outside, and inside, a pocket with divisions for pencils/pens/highlighters.

CONS:
1. Backpack adjustable straps: are on the lower part not allowing for easy adjustment while on your back
2. Lower connection backpack straps: hidden - cannot see whether sewn in well or not
3. Strap to hold computer in place: oddly long, which would allow for movement and sliding around, something you don't want your computer to do when inside
4. No compartment/pocket for a water bottle (my pet peeve)
5. PRIMARY (HUGE) ISSUE: Backpack straps which rest on upper trapezoids (left and right) are situated in a very uncomfortable position when fully loaded. I'm unsure if it's the angle or the placement, but the straps are too close to your neck and would cause pain. Primarily for this reason, I'm returning the backpack. Sad because even with the other cons (more annoyances than anything else) if it were not for this one, I would've kept the backpack because the pros outweigh the cons.

Pictures: It's important to see how a backpack will perform in my daily life. Therefore, the pictures provide a sense of how much stuff this can carry, with the contents both packed and unpacked.

Contents: Lenovo ThinkPad T460 in neoprene case, keys, 1 1/2" loose-leaf binder, yearly planner, scientific calculator, computer power cord, small cosmetic case, large cosmetic bag which houses pens/pencils/highlighters/usb drive/mouse/headphones and wallet.

Final thoughts: if only used as a briefcase/shoulder bag, this may be for you. However, if the primary purpose is to function as a backpack, good luck. I think another reviewer mentioned the oddly-placed backpack straps, but sadly, I ignored that advice.
